resolutions.researcher_notes: Natural Gas Intelligence (2014-10-31, live, fetched directly): 'The approximately $204 million pipeline has the capacity to deliver 200 MMcf/d of gas.' Mitsui & Co. press release (2013-12-05; live URL now 404, so cited via Wayback capture 20230921180310, confirmed to load and match text): 'The project will have a design capacity of approximately 200 million cubic feet per day.' AZCentral/Arizona Republic (2014-05-05; direct fetch 429 rate-limited, cited via Wayback capture 20211207065336, confirmed to load and match text): pipeline 'would carry up to 200 million cubic feet of gas a day.' Three distinct publishers (NGI, Mitsui, Gannett/Arizona Republic) independently agree on the 200 MMcf/d design capacity matching the sheet's value exactly -> high/independent. CONCERN (not a citation issue, informational only): Kinder Morgan's own current company overview PDF (pipeline2.kindermorgan.com/Documents/SGP/SGP_CI_Cpny_Overview.pdf, fetched directly, PDF text extracted) states Sierrita 'currently provides 523,640 dekatherms per day (Dth/d) of firm transportation capacity' following a stated 2020 expansion -- i.e. current actual capacity is materially higher than the sheet's 200 MMcf/d, which appears to reflect the pipeline's original 2014 design capacity only. Sheet value is well-sourced as the ORIGINAL capacity; flagging for a possible fills/status-review look at the 2020 expansion, not changing the value here.

NGI (2014, fetched directly): 'The 61-mile, 36-inch diameter lateral from El Paso Natural Gas's (EPNG) system in Arizona delivers to a point south of Tucson near the international border at Sasabe, AZ.' Kinder Morgan's own 2018 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, fetched directly with a compliant SEC User-Agent; full text searched): 'Near Tucson, Arizona, to the U.S.-Mexico border near Sasabe, Arizona; connects to EPNG and via an international border crossing with a third-party natural gas pipeline in Mexico.' Mitsui press release (via Wayback, confirmed loaded): 'extend south from Tucson to Sasabe in Arizona.' All corroborate the sheet's primary_value 'Tucson' and the Sasabe, Sonora, Mexico endpoint -> high/independent (3 distinct publishers: NGI, SEC filer Kinder Morgan, Mitsui). CONCERN: the sheet's `StartState/Province` field reads 'Texas', but every source found (NGI, KM's own 10-K, Mitsui, AZCentral, and KM's own current SGP overview PDF) places Tucson and the entire pipeline route in ARIZONA, not Texas -- Pima County, Tucson, and Sasabe are all Arizona locations. This looks like a data entry error on `StartState/Province` (should be Arizona). Not corrected here per the no-value-change rule; flagging for Update.

Mitsui & Co. press release (2013, via Wayback, confirmed loaded): 'its estimated project cost is approximately $200 million' -- matches the sheet's SegmentCost of $200,000,000 exactly. NGI (2014, fetched directly) and AZCentral (2014, via Wayback, confirmed loaded) both independently give '$204 million' for the completed/proposed pipeline. All three (Mitsui, NGI, Gannett/Arizona Republic) describe the same figure within ~2% of each other and of the sheet value (pre-construction estimate vs. later reported cost) -> high/independent. Sheet's $200,000,000 reads as the original Mitsui-sourced project estimate, which two later independent reports (NGI, AZCentral) essentially confirm at $204 million.
